Peepers
PEE-perz
noun (Silent Generation slang)
Peepers for "eyes" is long-standing English slang, centuries older than the Silent Generation, from peep, to look slyly or through a small opening. That generation knew it best from the 1938 song "Jeepers Creepers" (music by Harry Warren, words by Johnny Mercer), which asks a girl where she got "those peepers," and it stayed a fond, joking word for eyes through the 1940s and 1950s.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

When a crooner of 1938 asked a girl where she got "those peepers," the whole country hummed along, and Grandpa was still calling Grandma’s eyes her peepers fifty years later. It is a fond, homely word. Scripture has a great deal to say about the eyes, because they are the windows through which the heart is filled. "The light of the body is the eye" (Mat 6:22). Job made a solemn promise about his: "I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?" (Job 31:1). That is a word for every young man. The best use of our peepers is to look to God: "Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law" (Psa 119:18). And we should remember that our eyes are not the only ones watching: "The eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good" (Pro 15:3). That is a warning to the wicked and a comfort to the faithful. Grandchildren, God gave you your peepers as a gift. Use them to read His Word, to see the beauty of His world, and to notice the people around you who need help. And if you trust in Christ, one day you will use them to see Him face to face.

Webster 1828 Definition

Silent Generation slang (older English slang, made famous by a 1938 song) for the eyes — a fond word for a gift Scripture bids us guard: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid? (Job 31:1).

PEEPERS, n. pl. (old English slang; a Silent Generation favourite after a 1938 song) The eyes. "Close those peepers, young man — it’s past bedtime."

Decode for families: eyes; Job made a covenant with his, and David prayed for God to open his.

Key Scripture

Mat 6:22 — "The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light."

Job 31:1 — "I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?"

Psa 119:18 — "Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law."

Pro 15:3 — "The eyes of the LORD are in every place, beholding the evil and the good."

Modern Corruption

A wholesome, affectionate word for eyes; the only lesson is the one Scripture attaches to the eyes themselves — guard them.

expand to see more

There is nothing to correct in peepers. It is a grandparent’s word, said at bedtime and over a baby’s crib, and it is full of affection.

The word does open a door to one of Scripture’s plainest teachings: the eyes lead the heart. The song that made it famous was a young man admiring a girl’s eyes, which is innocent enough; but a covenant with the eyes, like Job’s, is what keeps admiration from becoming lust.

peep (to look slyly, through a small opening) → peeper (one who peeps) → slang peepers (the eyes) → 1938 song and 1940s–50s fond use.
